concepts.name: Life Processes
concepts.description: Learners should understand the four major life processes and their purpose in organisms.
concepts.evidence: The processes which together perform the maintenance job in living organisms are called life processes.

concepts.name: Autotrophic Nutrition
concepts.description: Learners should know how autotrophs make food via photosynthesis and its overall equation.
concepts.evidence: Photosynthesis is the process by which autotrophs take in carbon dioxide and water and convert them into carbohydrates in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll.

concepts.name: Heterotrophic Nutrition
concepts.description: Learners should differentiate holozoic, saprophytic, and parasitic modes of nutrition.
concepts.evidence: Heterotrophic nutrition can be holozoic, saprophytic or parasitic.

concepts.name: Human Digestion
concepts.description: Learners should describe the sequence of digestive organs, enzymes, and the role of peristalsis.
concepts.evidence: The lining of the canal has muscles that contract rhythmically to push food forward; these movements are called peristalsis.

concepts.name: Respiration Types
concepts.description: Learners should compare aerobic respiration with anaerobic fermentation and their products.
concepts.evidence: In yeast, without oxygen, pyruvate is converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide; this is anaerobic respiration (fermentation).

concepts.name: Human Respiratory System
concepts.description: Learners should understand the pathway of air, the role of alveoli, and the mechanics of breathing.
concepts.evidence: When we breathe in, the ribs lift and the diaphragm flattens, enlarging the chest cavity so air is sucked into the lungs.

concepts.name: Human Circulation
concepts.description: Learners should explain double circulation, heart chambers, and the functions of arteries, veins, and capillaries.
concepts.evidence: Because blood goes through the heart twice in each cycle, this is called double circulation; it keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood separate.

concepts.name: Plant Transport
concepts.description: Learners should describe xylem water movement and phloem translocation of photosynthates.
concepts.evidence: Xylem moves water and minerals obtained from the soil, and phloem transports the products of photosynthesis from the leaves to other parts of the plant.

concepts.name: Kidney Filtration
concepts.description: Learners should know the structure of a nephron and the role of Bowman's capsule and glomerulus in filtration.
concepts.evidence: Each kidney has large numbers of filtration units called nephrons. In each nephron, a cup-shaped end called Bowman's capsule surrounds a cluster of very thin-walled blood capillaries called the glomerulus, where blood is filtered.

concepts.name: Stomatal Control
concepts.description: Learners should understand how guard cells regulate opening and closing of stomata.
concepts.evidence: The opening and closing of each pore is controlled by guard cells: guard cells swell when water flows into them and the pore opens, and they shrink when they lose water and the pore closes.
